rule: Each blue (1) object slides horizontally and keeps its shape. Closed objects (solid blocks, or rings with a sealed hole) go to the left edge and become red (2). Open objects (a gap or missing side that lets background into a cavity, by the orthogonal-convex-hull test) go to the right edge and become green (3).
scope: Supported: grid width and height 10..30, 2-6 objects, each in its own band of rows separated by blank rows. Shapes are solid blocks or rectangular frames: hole 1-3 x 1-4, walls 1-2 thick, optional cut corners, optional top/bottom bumps on closed frames. Openings come from a missing wall side (C/U shape) or a through-gap of any length in one side. Every random scene has at least one open and one closed object. Fixed: background 4, input colour 1, output colours 2 (left) and 3 (right). Deliberately not supported: two objects sharing rows, irregular blob shapes, multiple holes, and multiple gaps per shape.
constraints: Objects occupy disjoint row bands with at least one blank row between bands, so the destinations at the left and right edges never overlap or touch.
Each object is a single 4-connected component and never touches another object, even diagonally.
Every random shape is checked for agreement between its intended open/closed label and a local hull-gap test on the isolated shape. Shapes that fail are rebuilt within bounded retries.
Corner cuts are applied only where both adjacent walls exist. Bumps avoid the corner columns, so a closed shape cannot become open by accident.
Every random scene contains at least one open and one closed object, and the colour change makes every example non-identity.
Each shape fits the grid: width at most min(W, 9) and height at most 7; the bands plus gaps fit within H.
known_limitations: The open/closed label is constructed, and a small local hull test is used only to reject inconsistent random constructions; it never reads the archived solver.
Fixtures are rebuilt from explicit per-object patterns with explicit side labels; the patterns were transcribed by hand from the canonical grids.
The shape family is rectangle-based frames and blocks, so arbitrary free-form outlines from the wider task concept are not produced.
Objects never share row bands, matching all canonical examples but excluding side-by-side layouts.
Bounded sampling raises instead of substituting a fixed scene.
